File table: The 1st entry of the FA table MUST be the root directory...
File table entry format: name_fmt: The format that the name length uses each increment doubles the number of bytes used in the name hash
lit_addr: The literal address of a file, offset to 0 being when the FAT table ends
name: A byte array containing the name's hash.

1st Stage (Clipping): Entries in both tables are validated by checking the file names they point to, hashing said name and if they are the same then simple link the two
If otherwise then temporarily remember (in RAM the hash at said location (As it may be corrupted)
2nd Stage (Who are you?): Each entry in the 1st FAT is compared against every other in the 2nd FAT
Hey, you're not in the other FAT table
Compare against the pointed location, if the hash at said location then sync to both FAT tables
3rd Stage, although Unneccessary(Chomp): This doesn't really make a diff as the FAT table is accessed Linearly
Although... It would be nice due the name hashes various size possibilities
Empty space (Marked empty as it's name_fmt == 0 or is 0d out)
Move whatever number of filled blocks are coming up next into that space

Directories: A file that has it's _attribute[0] set to 1
Directory file entry: _attributes: The private attributes of the file when considered in reference to the directory
This means that the following data should NOT be read as a Directory entry as it is arbitrary data
FAT_index (MUST not be 0!!!!): The index of the FAT table that holds this File's entry
name_len: The length of the name array, MUST point to a space character that is preceded by a normal character
Resolving a Directory's corruption: In the event that a Directory entry's FAT index does not point to the correct file entry of the same hash
If found, write to Directory's FAT index
If not found, then check 2nd FAT table
If found, write to Directory's FAT index
If not found, mark in Recovery Bin and remove from Directory
File convention: padding: padding to equalise size etc
name_fmt: The format of the name (sizeof(size_t) * 2^n)
creation_time: The creation time of the file [0 - 1](2 bytes): reserved, [2 - 5](4 bytes): Hr, [6 - 10](5 bytes): Min, [11 - 15](5 bytes): Sec
creation_date, MAX:= 365, MIN:= 0: The creation date of the file (In days of a yr)
access_date, MAX:= 365, MIN:= 0: last access/read date of the file (In days of a yr)
modified_time: The modified time of the file [0 - 1](2 bytes): reserved, [2 - 5](4 bytes): Hr, [6 - 10](5 bytes): Min, [11 - 15](5 bytes): Sec
modified_date, MAX:= 365, MIN:= 0: The modified date of the file (In days of a yr)
size: The size of the file
next_cluster_address:= The address of the next cluster(size_t), offset to 0 being when the FAT table ends
